events.text:
Added a "Running the tests" section to `README.md` on branch `docs/readme-test-instructions`, committed as `dde34a8`.

What I documented, and the assumption behind it:

- The repo has **no tests and no test tooling** — no `tests/` directory, no `pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`tox.ini`, no CI config. So there was no existing command to document.
- I wrote the section against **pytest with tests under `tests/`**, the default convention for a plain Python project like this one. The example paths (`tests/test_pricing_cache.py`) are illustrative, not real files.
- I included an explicit note in the README that no suite exists yet, so a reader running `pytest` and seeing "no tests ran" isn't confused by docs that overstate reality.

I did not run the commands, since there is nothing for them to collect. If you'd rather the README reflect a different runner (unittest, tox, a `make test` target), tell me which and I'll rewrite it — or I can scaffold an actual `tests/` directory with tests for `reconcile`, `lookup`, and `plan` so the section describes something real.

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 7505656..ac1deca 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -1 +1,21 @@
 # fixture repo
+
+## Running the tests
+
+Tests are run with [pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/):
+
+```sh
+pip install pytest
+pytest
+```
+
+Run a single file or a single test with:
+
+```sh
+pytest tests/test_pricing_cache.py
+pytest tests/test_pricing_cache.py::test_lookup_falls_back_to_snapshot
+```
+
+> **Note:** this repo does not have a test suite yet. The commands above
+> describe the intended convention (pytest, tests under `tests/`); they will
+> report "no tests ran" until tests are added.
